newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs end firm on BOJ rate remark.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs end firm on BOJ rate remark.

text.p: Comments by Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita gave a lift to SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) on Monday, helping the market shrug off Japan's August industrial production data which matched expectations.

Matsushita's comment that the fall in long-term interest rates might reflect changing sentiment about Japan's economic prospects appeared to deny a Friday wire report that the BOJ was concerned about excessively low long-term rates.
March Euroyen rose on the back of the comment, and was propelled to a new high of 99.25 by stop-loss buying and short-covering later in the day, dealers said.
"The industrial production data had been much awaited. But when it came out, the market barely budged," said a trader with an Asian futures house.
He said March Euroyen faced resistance around 99.25/26 and 99.28. "It's looking quite toppish already."
The contract ended at 99.22 against its CME close at 99.20. December JGBs settled at 122.13 against their opening 121.60.
Eurodollar futures finished slightly firmer on the back of gains in U.S. bonds, but activity was subdued as players looked ahead to the release of key U.S. economic data.
The market will scrutinise the National Association of Purchasing Management index and the September jobs report for signs of inflation later this week, dealers said.
December Eurodollars closed at 94.25 against their IMM settlement at 94.23. March closed at 94.11 against 94.10.
